Zero-G Firewall.

An interactive fire lab built on NASA’s microgravity experiments.

Overview

What happens to a flame when a spacecraft’s fans stop? Built for NASA Space Apps Sofia, Zero-G Firewall lets readers start from a question, compare test conditions and follow a result to its original NASA table. A separate alarm exercise pairs a recording from the Saffire-III experiment with clearly identified simulated scenarios.

An experiment behind a number

In Fire Lab, choose a FLEX droplet to see its fuel, oxygen fraction, pressure and starting diameter. Model Lab takes those conditions to a separate screen with a burning-rate estimate. The experimental record and the model output have different roles.

A limit the reader can test

The evaluation groups repeat observations by regime. Holding out a regime tests transfer to unseen experimental conditions. A material or gravity setting outside the training domain can lead the interface to withhold a numerical prediction.

More screens

Capabilities

  • Browse 24 combustion investigations and export the real tests nearest to a chosen set of conditions.
  • Explore a droplet burning-rate model trained on 257 eligible FLEX rows. Validation keeps repeated observations from each of the 78 experimental regimes together.
  • Inspect data provenance and compare experimental results with a Three.js fire simulation.

One workflow

  1. NASA tables
  2. Group test regimes
  3. Evaluate predictions

Data and output

Development

The November 2026 build grew from an evidence browser into a lab with in-browser prediction, a 3D scene and a signed data release.
